To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the biotransformations induced by white-rot basidiomycetes in lignocellulosics wastes are affected by the aeration rate, and that these changes are related to the mineralization and the humification processes.
aeration has no effect on lignin degradation and humification by the white-rot fungi Coriolus versiclor and Phanerochaetf flavido-alba.
The mineralisation of organic matter in sterile horticulture plant wastes inoculated by Coriolus versicolour and Phanerochaetes flavido-alba is affected by different aeration rates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the inoculation of lignocellulolytic fungi on composting processes.
the use of lignocellulolytic fungi for the biodegradation of plant wastes.
the effect of different aeration rates on the biotrasformation of lignocellular wastes by white- rot fungi.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mineralisation and humification of organic material in the presence of white-rot fungi are strongly influenced by the aeration rates.
the two fungi are equally efficient in lignin biodegradation, while P. flavidoalba is more effective in mineralisation and C. versicolor in humification of lignocellulose.
the two fungi studied are able to mineralise and humify lignocellulosics wastes, but the mineralisation of OM is more effectively carried out under low aeration conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fungi analysed may facilitate waste composting by means of an enhanced substrate bioavailability and an increased OM humification.
aeration is important for the mineralisation process, but not for the humification process.

the two fungi analysed may be used as inoculants in the composting process to increase the mineralisation of OM and the humification process, but the effect on composting is more noticeable in the case of C. versicolor than in the case of P. flavidoalba.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two fungi studied can be used to enhance lignin degradation and humification during composting of lignin rich wastes.
aeration rate is critical to achieve a high level of mineralisation and a low level of humification of lignocellulose wastes by white- rot fungi.
aeration has a positive effect on the degradation of lignocellulose, and therefore, the use of white-rot fungi for the treatment of lignocellulous wastes is recommended.
